text.p: The Patriot American Hospitality Inc talks with Wyndham Hotel Corp that led to Monday's merger announcement began about six weeks ago, although the two chief executives have known each other for five years, Patriot Chairman Paul A. Nussbaum said.
In late February, Wyndham said it had hired Smith Barney to assist its review of alternatives following press reports of talks with Patriot.
Wyndham was "aware of other companies interested in us," Chairman James D. Carreker told a teleconference Monday, adding "We wanted to select a long-term partner."
He said initial Wyndham international expansion will be north and south, into Canada and Mexico, where the company feels it has the best brand leverage.
Carreaker called Mexico "a natural expansion of our Caribbean presence," adding "Mexico's the next destination stop for us."
Nussbaum said Crow family interests and Wyndham managment holding a total of 59 percent of the company's stock have agreed to vote in favor of the merger.
Noting the Crow family now holders about 47 percent of Wyndham's stock, Carreker said this would be diluted to "roughly 14 percent" of the merged company.

Nussbaum said some of the Crow family holding would be in a special class of stock so as to not violate the company's REIT tax advantage. Noting this would be lost if more than 9.8 percent of a REIT's stock were in the hands of one holder, he described this as a takeover defense.
Nussbaum also said Patriot's agreement with Hilton Hotels Corp to develop Hilton Garden units had ended on its own terms.
Some of the sites acquired for use as Hilton Garden units may be used for Wyndham Garden hotels, he added.
